newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU SAYS 1,600 TONNES UK BEEF EXPORTED ILLEGALLY.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU SAYS 1,600 TONNES UK BEEF EXPORTED ILLEGALLY.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday that 1,600 tonnes of British beef had illegally been exported to the Netherlands, Russia and Egypt despite a ban imposed because of the mad cow crisis.

Seven hundred tonnes had been seized by Dutch authorities after being exported via Belgium and the remaining 900 tonnes had probably been exported to Russia and Egypt, said Nikolaus van der Pas, spokesman for the Commission.
Van der Pas denied press reports that British beef had been fraudulently marketed in France and Spain and could not confirm reports of exports to other third countries such as Bosnia.

The Commission said on Wednesday it was considering legal action against Britain over the exports which were banned in March 1996 to protect consumer health after the British government said it was possible a human form of the fatal mad cow disease, CJD, could be caught from eating infected beef.
But it sparked outrage by refusing to say how much beef was involved and to which countries it had been exported.

On Thursday it changed that, although EU Food Safety Commissioner Emma Bonino told Italian TV on Wednesday that "British beef was found to have been exported to Belgium, France, Spain and the Netherlands."
The Commission's announcement followed an EU veterinary inspectors' mission last week to Britain, which included visits to sea ports.
Van der Pas said the British beef sold in the Netherlands had been marketed as being from Belgium.
He said the Commission was pleased that concern over the illegal exports had prompted a tightening up of inspections by EU authorities.
He said also that he had no information on press reports suggesting a syndicate of British army troops were involved in the beef scam.
